title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 75
paragraphs: Just as the armies were about to join battle, the Corinthians first, reflecting among themselves that they were not acting rightly, changed their minds and went away; and after that Demaratus son of Ariston, who was king of the Spartans along with Cleomenes, did the same, though he had joined with him in leading the army out from Lacedaemon and had not up to this point been at variance with Cleomenes. Because of this dissension a law was laid down at Sparta that it should not be permitted, when an army went out, for both kings to go with it—for up to this time both used to go—and that as one of the kings was released from service, so one of the sons of Tyndareus too should be left behind; for before this, both of these were called on for help and went with the armies.
